entities.name: Paris Uprising of 1832
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Paris Uprising of 1832 was a pivotal event in modern history that shook the very foundations of the French capital. 

 On June 5, 1832, a group of insurgents, largely composed of students and workers, took to the streets of Paris, sparking a wave of protests and riots that would last for several days. 

 The uprising was led by a coalition of liberal and socialist groups, who were determined to overthrow the conservative government of King Louis-Philippe. Armed with a combination of swords, pistols, and pikes, the rebels clashed with government forces in a series of bloody battles, leaving hundreds dead and thousands injured. 

 The aftermath of the uprising saw a significant increase in government repression, with the imposition of martial law and the arrest of hundreds of suspected rebels. 

 The Paris Uprising of 1832 may have been crushed, but its legacy continued to shape the course of French history, influencing the development of the next generation of revolutionaries, including the likes of Louis Blanc and Karl Marx, who drew inspiration from the uprising's ideals of social justice and equality.
